subject: social_science
chapter_title: Money and Credit: Banks, Loans and Terms of Credit

concepts.title: Money as a Medium of Exchange and Double Coincidence of Wants
concepts.section: Money as a Medium of Exchange
concepts.definition: Money removes the need for a double coincidence of wants by acting as an intermediate step: a seller converts goods into money and then buys whatever is desired, unlike barter where each party must want exactly what the other offers.
concepts.key_idea: A shoe manufacturer need not find a wheat-growing farmer who also wants shoes; selling shoes for money and buying wheat with money completes both exchanges.
question_patterns: how does the use of money make it easier to exchange things
what is double coincidence of wants
explain the barter system and its limitation
why does everyone prefer to receive payments in money
how does money act as an intermediate in the exchange process
give an example of goods exchanged through barter

solution_steps.explain: Check whether goods are swapped directly (barter) or sold for money that then buys other goods (medium of exchange).
In barter, both parties must agree to sell and buy each other's commodities; money removes this requirement.
Confirm the two-step route: producer sells output for money, then uses money to buy inputs or food, as in shoes for money for wheat.

concepts.title: Modern Forms of Money: Currency and Demand Deposits
concepts.definition: Modern money takes two linked forms: currency, meaning paper notes and coins authorised by the government and issued by the Reserve Bank of India, and demand deposits with banks that can be withdrawn on demand and paid by cheque.
concepts.key_idea: The rupee cannot be legally refused in settling transactions in India, and cheque payments transfer money between accounts without cash, so deposits share the essential features of money.
question_patterns: why is modern currency accepted as a medium of exchange
who is authorised to issue currency notes in india
what are demand deposits and why are they called money
how is payment made through a cheque
can any individual legally refuse a payment made in rupees
how did salim pay the leather supplier without cash

solution_steps.explain: Identify whether the money held is currency (notes and coins) or a bank deposit withdrawable on demand.
Confirm the Reserve Bank of India issues notes on behalf of the central government and the law legalises rupee payments.
Follow the instruction route: payer's cheque directs the bank to pay a specific amount into the payee's account, completing payment without cash.

concepts.title: Loan Activities of Banks and the Interest Spread
concepts.definition: Banks keep only a small slice of deposits as cash, lend the major portion to borrowers, and earn their main income from the difference between the higher interest charged on loans and the lower interest paid to depositors.
concepts.key_idea: Banks mediate between depositors with surplus funds and borrowers who need them; Indian banks hold roughly 5 per cent of deposits as cash to meet withdrawals.
question_patterns: how do banks earn their main source of income
what do banks do with the deposits they accept
why do banks keep only a small proportion of deposits as cash
how do banks mediate between depositors and borrowers
between which two interest rates is the difference the bank's income
what happens if all depositors demand money at the same time

solution_steps.explain: Separate the small cash reserve kept for withdrawals from the major portion extended as loans.
Confirm the loan rate charged to borrowers is higher than the deposit rate paid to depositors.
Show that this difference, or spread, is the bank's main income, earned while channelling surplus funds to loan demand.

concepts.title: Bank Cash Reserve from Deposit Percentage
concepts.definition: The cash a bank holds for daily withdrawals equals its total deposits multiplied by the reserve percentage it maintains.
concepts.key_idea: Holding about 5 per cent of deposits as cash works because on any given day only some depositors come to withdraw money.
question_patterns: calculate the cash reserve a bank keeps from its deposits
find the amount held as cash when the reserve percentage is given
what percentage of deposits do indian banks hold as cash
compute the cash provision for withdrawals from total deposits
why can a bank manage with a small cash reserve

solution_steps.explain: Multiply total deposits by the cash reserve percentage and divide by 100

concepts.title: Two Different Credit Situations and the Debt Trap
concepts.definition: Credit helps when production and earnings rise, as with Salim's festival-season order, but pushes the borrower into a debt trap when repayment fails, as when Swapna's pest-hit groundnut crop forced her to sell part of her land.
concepts.key_idea: Whether credit is useful depends on the risks in the situation and whether there is support in case of loss.
question_patterns: compare the credit situations of salim and swapna
what is a debt trap and how does it arise
when does credit play a positive role
why did swapna have to sell part of her land
what risks decide whether credit is useful or harmful
how did salim use credit to increase his earnings

solution_steps.explain: Distinguish working capital credit that raises earnings from distress credit taken for cultivation costs or daily expenses.
See whether income from the activity covered the loan: Salim repaid and profited, while Swapna's crop failure left the debt growing.
Confirm the spiral: fresh loans to repay old ones, then forced sale of assets such as land, marking the debt trap.

concepts.title: Terms of Credit: Interest, Collateral and Documentation
concepts.definition: Every loan agreement fixes terms of credit: the interest rate on the principal, collateral as an asset pledged as guarantee, documentation requirements, and the mode of repayment such as monthly instalments.
concepts.key_idea: Megha's five lakh house loan at 12 per cent annual interest for ten years used the new house papers as collateral; borrowers always look for low interest, easy repayment and less collateral.
question_patterns: what do the terms of credit include
why do lenders ask for collateral while lending
what is collateral and give its examples
what are the terms of megha's house loan
what does easy terms of credit mean for a borrower
how does the mode of repayment differ across loans

solution_steps.explain: Check the agreement for interest rate, collateral, documentation requirement and mode of repayment.
Collateral such as land titles, bank deposits or livestock lets the lender sell the asset if the borrower fails to repay.
Place Megha's loan details against the terms: 12 per cent annual rate, 10-year monthly instalments, house papers retained, salary documents submitted.

concepts.title: Annual Interest from the Monthly Rate
concepts.definition: Informal lenders in villages quote monthly rates, and the yearly burden follows by multiplying the monthly interest rate by twelve, as in the moneylender's five per cent per month equal to 60 per cent per annum.
concepts.key_idea: Shyamal paid 60 per cent a year to the moneylender before shifting to a trader's three per cent per month, while Arun's bank loan costs only 8.5 per cent per annum.
question_patterns: convert a monthly interest rate into an annual rate
calculate the per annum rate when the per month rate is given
what is 5 per cent per month as an annual rate
compare the moneylender's and the bank's annual interest rates
find the yearly interest burden of a village loan
why is informal credit costlier than bank credit for shyamal

solution_steps.action: scale the rate to a year
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the monthly interest rate percentage by 12 to get the annual rate percentage

concepts.title: Simple Interest on a Loan
concepts.definition: The interest payable on a loan grows with the principal, the annual interest rate and the time period, following the simple interest relation used to cost any credit arrangement.
concepts.key_idea: Megha's loan of Rs 5 lakh at 12 per cent per annum shows how interest adds to the repayment burden on top of the principal.
question_patterns: calculate the interest on a loan for the given rate and period
find the interest payable on a house loan
how much interest does a loan of principal at rate percent for years carry
compute the total interest cost of borrowing
what interest accrues on megha's loan in one year
work out the interest amount from principal rate and time

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the principal by the annual rate percent and the number of years, then divide by 100

concepts.title: Formal and Informal Sources of Credit
concepts.definition: Loans come from the formal sector of banks and cooperatives or from informal lenders such as moneylenders, traders, employers, relatives and friends; the Reserve Bank of India supervises only the formal sector.
concepts.key_idea: Commercial banks supply 51 per cent of rural credit and moneylenders 23 per cent; informal lending charges much more, has no supervision, and can drag borrowers into debt and debt traps.
question_patterns: distinguish between formal and informal sources of credit
who supervises the functioning of formal sources of loans
why is the cost of informal loans much higher
which is the largest formal source of credit in rural india
why do banks and cooperative societies need to lend more
why can nobody stop informal lenders from using unfair means

solution_steps.explain: Formal sector means banks and cooperatives; informal covers moneylenders, traders, employers, relatives and friends.
The RBI monitors bank cash balances and lending patterns; no organisation supervises informal lenders, so they can charge whatever interest they choose.
Higher borrowing costs leave borrowers less income, can exceed earnings, and deter enterprise, which is why cheap formal credit must expand.

concepts.title: Formal Share of Rural Household Credit
concepts.definition: The share of rural household credit supplied by the formal sector is found by adding the bank and cooperative shares, and the formal credit amount is that share of the total rural borrowing.
concepts.key_idea: Commercial banks (51 per cent), cooperative banks and societies (10 per cent) and other formal agencies (5 per cent) together meet about two-thirds of rural credit needs.
question_patterns: calculate the formal sector share of rural credit
find the credit amount supplied by banks and cooperatives together
what per cent of rural household credit comes from the formal sector
compute the money lent by the formal sector from total rural borrowing
which agencies make up the formal share of credit
is more rural credit coming from the formal or informal sector

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the total rural credit by the combined formal sector percentage and divide by 100

concepts.title: Self Help Groups and Grameen Bank
concepts.section: Self Help Groups for the Poor
concepts.definition: Self Help Groups pool the savings of 15 to 20 members, mostly women, lend from the pooled fund, and later qualify for bank loans in the group's name, while the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh pioneered similar group lending for the poor.
concepts.key_idea: SHGs let members get timely loans at reasonable interest without collateral, and help women become financially self-reliant, building blocks of rural social capital.
question_patterns: how do self help groups help borrowers overcome lack of collateral
how many members does a typical shg have
explain the working of shgs in rural areas
what is the grameen bank of bangladesh famous for
why are shgs called the building blocks of rural social capital
what kinds of loans do shg members take and for what

solution_steps.explain: Members of 15-20 person groups save regularly and the pooled savings fund small loans to members.
After a record of timely repayment, the group becomes eligible for bank loans in its name, which it on-lends to members.
Confirm benefits: loans without collateral at fair interest, timely credit for production needs, and greater self-reliance for women members.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A bank holds total deposits of {total_deposits} lakh rupees and keeps {reserve_percent} per cent of them as cash. Calculate the cash reserve the bank maintains.

solution_template.action: scale the rate to a year

worked_examples.question_pattern: Rural households borrowed {rural_credit_total} crore rupees in a year. Using the survey share of {formal_share_percent} per cent for the formal sector, calculate the credit supplied by banks and cooperatives together.

solution_template.explain: Multiply the total rural credit by the combined formal sector percentage and divide by 100

worked_examples.question_pattern: A district's rural borrowing totals {rural_credit_total} lakh rupees and the formal sector meets {formal_share_percent} per cent of it. Find the formal sector credit of the district.
